sec-head.h2: When vLLM is not the right choice

p: If your workload is purely low-latency (<50ms) single-request inference with small models, a simpler solution like Hugging Face TGI or a direct ONNX runtime may be cheaper and easier. vLLM shines under high throughput, large models, and dynamic batching. For fully managed needs, consider OpenAI or Anthropic APIs instead of self-hosted LLM serving.

faq-item.faq-q: What is the difference between vLLM and Hugging Face TGI?
faq-item.faq-a: vLLM uses PagedAttention for near-zero memory waste and higher throughput under concurrent requests. TGI supports simpler batching and is easier to set up for small models. vLLM is the better choice for large models and high-throughput serving.

faq-item.faq-q: Do I need a vLLM consultant, or can I deploy it myself?
faq-item.faq-a: Basic deployment is straightforward, but optimizing throughput, GPU utilization, and cost per token often requires deep experience with scheduling, tensor parallelism, and KV cache sizing. A consultant accelerates production readiness and avoids costly mistakes.

faq-item.faq-q: How much do vLLM deployment services cost?
faq-item.faq-a: A single model deployment typically runs $2,500 to $7,000. A full production serving setup ranges from $10,000 to $35,000+ depending on model size and parallelism. Hourly consulting is $100 to $200/hr.
Yes, vLLM is open-source under the Apache 2.0 license. There are no licensing fees, but you pay for GPU compute. Our services focus on maximizing throughput per GPU to reduce your serving costs.

faq-item.faq-q: When should I NOT use vLLM?
faq-item.faq-a: If you need sub-50ms latency for single requests with small models, a simpler framework like TGI or ONNX Runtime may be more cost-effective. vLLM excels under high throughput, dynamic batching, and large model serving.
